items.title: Vida y peligros de un detective hoy: “No quiero más sectas, me metí en una y casi me enganchan”
items.description: A Gómez, hombre casado de 39 años, unos conocidos le sorprendieron paseando con otra mujer a las tres de la madrugada en las ferias de Talavera. “Es una cosa muy dura. La presenté como mi amiga, pero notaba cómo estaban teniendo cortocircuitos en el cerebro. Sales de cervezas a las tantas con una señora que no es la tuya y, claro, la gente se bloquea”, lamenta. “Lo que ellos no saben es que yo no cometo infidelidades. ¡Las investigo!”. Al frente del despacho Wolf and Wolf Detectives, Gómez ejerce como investigador privado desde el municipio de la provincia de Toledo y, a menudo, se asocia con una colega, Herminia, de 40 años, que tiene también su propia agencia, Herminia AC, Detective & Criminóloga. En aquella ocasión, no perseguían una infidelidad, sino a una persona que estaba trabajando en la feria mientras se encontraba de baja en otra empresa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tomando cañas y pornografiando la miseria
items.description: Los rascacielos son la erección del poder económico. En Manhattan hay muchos, pero a pie de calle se pasea la más absoluta pobreza, tanta y tan frecuente que ya forma parte del paisaje, como las montañas de basura, las columnas de humo que salen del asfalto o los spaghetti meatballs en esos diners en peligro de extinción. Si uno va a Nueva York y no se ha topado con la mirada enloquecida de un homeless que predica el apocalipsis, si no se ha cruzado con los pasos silenciosos de una bag lady que empuja un carrito con todas sus pertenencias, es como si no hubiera estado en Nueva York . items.title: El DIN A4 de Mourinho
items.description: El veinteañero irrumpe en la habitación sin pensarlo. No importa que sean las nueve de la noche o, lo que es lo mismo, plena madrugada para cualquier madre de familia. Necesita enseñar algo de manera urgente. “Mira, mira”, repite, casi aplastando el móvil en la cara de su interlocutora. El objeto de tanta excitación es el papel impreso DIN A4, a todo color, con dos jugadas de fútbol que blande José Mourinho en una rueda de prensa después de que el Real Madrid pierda el derbi contra el Atlético. “Es increíble”, repite el chaval, regodeándose con los vídeos de TikTok que se mofan del entrenador, que se defiende a la antigua, con papel y boli. items.description: Desde la reunificación alemana, los conservadores y socialdemócratas se han alternado siempre en el poder como los partidos más votados en Berlín. Hasta el pasado domingo . El partido de Die Linke (La Izquierda) ha dejado de estar limitado tradicionalmente a los barrios del este para alzarse como el partido más votado de Berlín impulsado por una campaña centrada, principalmente, en la lucha contra la escasez y los precios de la vivienda. La germano-turca Elif Eralp puede convertirse así en la primera alcaldesa de Berlín de la formación izquierdista, aunque para lograrlo necesitará un acuerdo de coalición con ecologistas y socialdemócratas. items.title: Plan Alquila Madrid: la web “prehistórica” de la Comunidad para encontrar casa de alquiler que cuesta 750.000 euros anuales
items.description: Si usted busca un piso para alquilar en la Comunidad de Madrid, hay un enlace con el logo oficial del Gobierno madrileño que le invita a entrar en la web del Plan Alquila. Si se hace clic, se avanzará hasta una página web fundada en el año 2008. Una página web de letras diminutas, casi ilegibles. Puede que la inteligencia artificial avance a un ritmo vertiginoso, pero la web del Plan Alquila —por la que la Comunidad paga 750.000 euros al año a la empresa Factoría Digital por la gestión e ideada para facilitar el alquiler de los madrileños— lleva otros ritmos, está detenida en el tiempo desde hace casi dos décadas. Eso sí, el Plan Alquila tiene un mapa gigantesco con toda la región que promete mostrarle todas las ofertas disponibles. Un mapa que está roto. Un mapa que no funciona. Un mapa vacío: según el mapa, no hay ninguna vivienda en alquiler en la región madrileña. Un mapa de viviendas de alquiler en la Comunidad de Madrid donde no hay ni una sola vivienda de alquiler en la Comunidad de Madrid. Solo si se fija usted en una pequeña pestaña con el nombre de “Listado” podrá ver que en estos momentos Plan Alquila tiene “anunciadas” 140 casas en la capital y otras tantas en diversos municipios. Por desgracia, esto tampoco es así. Un porcentaje significativo son inmuebles que ya están alquilados, aunque aquí aparezcan como disponibles. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Trabajo propone un programa público para que 200.000 jóvenes accedan a su primer empleo hasta 2028
items.description: El Ministerio de Trabajo ha abierto este lunes una nueva mesa de diálogo social con los sindicatos y la patronal para rediseñar las políticas activas de empleo destinadas a los colectivos de jóvenes y parados de larga duración de más edad (de entre 45 y más de 55 años, según la medida) a partir del año que viene. Estas políticas incluyen formación, incentivos a la contratación o mejoras en los procesos de búsqueda de empleo e intermediación laboral. Entre las principales novedades para los más jóvenes, Trabajo propone un Programa de primera experiencia profesional , con acciones específicas de los servicios públicos de empleo e itinerarios personalizados específicos que se coloca como meta que al menos 200.000 jóvenes hayan accedido a su primer empleo para 2028. Estos puestos podrán ubicarse tanto en el sector privado como en el público. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Gobierno y la Junta retrasan la declaración como sobreexplotados de los acuíferos andaluces, pese a que muchos se secan
items.description: El nivel de muchos acuíferos andaluces está en caída libre pese al respiro temporal que supusieron las copiosas lluvias del año pasado. Cada vez más comarcas del interior sufren para mantener el abastecimiento de su población ante la merma de sus masas subterráneas. Para sobrevivir a esta alarmante escasez, el primer paso es declarar el acuífero “en riesgo”, denominación actual de sobreexplotado, para así primar las extracciones esenciales para el consumo humano, condicionar las recreativas y atajar de una vez los pozos ilegales. Es decir, poner orden para saber cómo se ha esquilmado el subsuelo hídrico. De momento, en la región hay seis acuíferos declarados sobreexplotados, según cifras oficiales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Chinese visitors to Gilgit-Baltistan may get visa on arrival
items.description: • Proposal for entry to Hunza, Nagar discussed at SIFC •One-window NOC portal to streamline clearance at Sost • Final rollout pending clearance from higher authorities GILGIT: Pakistan is considering special visa-on-arrival arrangements for Chinese tourists travelling to Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass, with officials proposing a pilot programme initially covering Hunza and Nagar districts to promote cross-border tourism and economic activity. The proposal was discussed during a high-level meeting titled “Restora­t­i­­on of Visa Facility on Arri­val at Sost for Chinese Tou­rists” held at the Special In­­­vestment Facilitation Council (SIFC) Secretariat at the Prime Minister’s Office in Islamabad on Sept 15. The session, chaired by the joint secretary for SW-B at the SIFC, brought together officials from the Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) home and tourism departments, the Pakistan Tourism De­­v­elopment Corporation, the ministries of inter-provincial coordination, interior and foreign affairs, Pakis­t­­an Association of Tour Ope­­rators (Pato) and Green Tourism Pakistan Limited. According to the meeting minutes, the foreign affairs ministry expressed no objection in principle to the proposal, subject to security clearance. The interior ministry, however, noted that visa-on-arrival access had been suspended for all countr­i­­es after security concerns prompted a policy change at the highest level, and said any exception for Chi­nese nationals would need approval at the same level. Delegates from the Fed­e­­­ration of Pakistan Cham­bers of Commerce and Ind­ustry (FPCCI) argued that expanding Chinese tourism could boost foreign ex­­c­­hange earnings, create jobs and stimulate local economies, at a time when Pakistan is seeking greater foreign investment. Officials and stakeholders from GB proposed that a special or trial arrangement for Chinese tourists could be considered. They said tourism underpinned livelihoods across the region and that a downturn in visitor numbers, driven by wider global instability, had hit local businesses hard. Officials pointed to Hunza-Nagar’s existing tourism infrastructure and said no significant security threat had been identified along the proposed route. The GB government expressed willingness to provide security arrangements for tourists. Raja Nazimul Amin, adviser to the president on international trade and tourism investment at FPCCI, who attended the meeting, told Dawn that all relevant stakeholders had agreed to special arrangements for on-arrival visas for Chinese tourists travelling through the Khunj­erab Pass in phases. “Initially, it has been proposed that the visa on arrival will be given to Chinese tourists up to Hunza and Nagar districts under phase one,” Amin said. “If the trial basis remains successful, then it would be extended to the whole of Gilgit-Baltistan in phase two.” Mr Amin said the plan could generate billions of dollars in economic activity. He said the recommendations would be forwar­d­­ed to Prime Minister She­hbaz Sharif for appro­val, which he expected to be granted. Meanwhile, the Minis­try of Inter-Provincial Coordi­nation (MOIPC) called for the visa process to be stre­amlined, proposing a single online portal for no-objection certificates (NOCs). The GB Home Depart­m­ent, which currently issues NOCs through a multi-step police clearance process, agreed to explore a more efficient one-window system at Sost. The SIFC has asked the GB government to submit a detailed proposal. The plan will then go to MOIPC, before being referred to the interior and foreign ministries for concurrence and passed to higher authorities for a final decision. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: 4 terrorists die in Panjgur intelligence-based operation: officials
items.description: QUETTA: Security forces killed four more terrorists belonging to a banned organisation in an intelligence-based operation carried out in two areas of Panjgur district, officials said on Monday. According to officials, security forces launched an IBO on the information about the presence of armed militants in Koh-Prom and the Aphan area of Panjgur district. “Four armed terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan were killed in the heavy gunbattle during the operation,” they said, adding that a large quantity of arms and ammunition was seized from the hideouts of the terrorists. During the last one week, security forces have killed more than 35 terrorists in multiple actions conducted in several parts of Balochistan under the Radd-ul-Fitna operation. Search for kidnapped Kharan DC continues; two cricketers abducted from Dera Bugti Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti praised the security personnel for the successful operation against militants in Panjgur. He said that these operations would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism and that the government was pursuing a policy of zero tolerance against elements hostile to the country. Search operation underway Meanwhile, investigators have found no clue to the whereabouts of the Kharan deputy commissioner, who was kidnapped alongside three others two days ago. DC Munir Soomro and three other people were kidnapped as they were travelling in a car the other day. Officials said that police and other security personnel were searching different areas to recover Mr Soomro, but had made no headway so far. They said that Mr Soomro was heading to Kharan from Quetta along with his driver, a guard and another person in a private car. The armed men intercepted his car in Lajah area of Kharan district and took it along with their car. Police said that after receiving information about the missing deputy commissioner, several attempts were made to establish a contact with him through his cellphone, but his phone was found silent. The provincial administration has involved tribal elders of the area to contact the kidnappers for their safe release, but no progress has been made. Meanwhile, two local cricketers were kidnapped near the Kachhi Canal area in Dera Bugti. According to police, Zakir and Wadan Bugti, residents of Sui, were returning home after playing a match in Kandhkot when they were stopped by armed men near the Kachhi Canal area. After their abduction, security personnel cordoned off the area and launched a search operation. No one has claimed responsibility for the kidnapping of the two cricketers so far. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Govt tactics pushing people towards revolt: Fazl
items.description: ISLAMABAD: With the country facing mounting debt pressure and inflation, the government’s attempt to lock down the federal capital to counter protests will only encourage rebellious tendencies among the people, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman said. Speaking at a news conference at his residence on Monday after a central council meeting of his party, the JUI-F chief demanded that parliament should be taken into confidence on important national and foreign policy issues noting that the country was passing through a critical juncture. The JUI-F chief also called for an in-camera session of parliament on the regional security situation. The Maulana said some political parties had announced protests, but the government had filled Islamabad with containers ahead of the demonstrations. “By adopting such tactics, you are creating rebels yourself,” he said. JUI-F chief demands in-camera session of parliament on govt policies, regional security situation He said the PTI decided to hold protests and it was its right to do so. He recalled that the JUI-F had staged long marches in the past without causing damage to public property, saying even the Metro Bus service had continued to ply during the Lahore March. ‘Mediation role’ When asked by journalists, the JUI-F chief turned down the mediation offer and said that his party had reservations about this government. “We are an opposition party. How can we mediate?” he asked. He said dialogue could take place when there is a representative of the government. “The government should talk to those who are protesting. We ourselves are a party to the political dispute,” he said. The JUI-F chief said his party considered the hybrid government nothing but a representative of the military establishment and stressed that political dialogue required a government with genuine political authority. “We have decided to raise these issues from our own platform because economy and inflation are issues concerning everyone,” he said. The Maulana condemned the arrest of PTI founder’s sisters, saying political workers and parties should be allowed to exercise their constitutional right to hold protest rallies. He also criticised the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning circumstances in which a provincial minister was allegedly shot and taken away. Referring to reports about possible constitutional amendments, the JUI-F chief said he would welcome provincial autonomy, but added that the issue should be discussed in the context of the constitutional position that existed 25 years ago. He said the party had played a key role in difficult circumstances in the past, recalling that in 2003 it spent 10 days working to help bring Pakistan-India relations out of a quagmire. He said the role played at that time should also be kept in view while discussing the political and diplomatic options available at the present. He alleged that the country had lost the confidence of Beijing. According to him, state institutions are in a defensive position while the country is facing serious internal challenges. “The country is in difficulty and we are sitting on a powder keg,” he said, adding that the issues confronting the country should be brought before the parliament. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Houthis push for control of Yemen’s highlands
items.description: • Trump speaks with Yemen’s president, doesn’t pledge military support • NYT says US president reversed decision on air strikes on Houthis DUBAI: Houthi fighters were pushing to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute. US President Trump spoke by phone with Yem­eni President Rashad al-Alimi on Sun­day, four people familiar with the matter said, discussing the advances of the Houthis around a vital global waterway. Alimi requested US support for his Saudi-backed government in its fight against the Houthis, who this month took key areas along the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive. Two of the sources, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump had made no direct pledge of military support during the call. The White House and Yemen’s information minister did not immediately respond to requests for comment. On the other hand, a lightning advance by the Houthis this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre. Strategic heights Five Yemeni military sources told Reu­ters that the Houthis were now seeking to seize strategic heights, known as the Kah­b­oub Mountains, in two provinces, Taiz and Lahij, which separate the Red Sea coast from the government-held south. Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote mountain Al-Wazi’iyah district in Taiz province, and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast between the mouth of the Red Sea that the fighters captured last week and the government’s base in Aden. The Houthis aim to secure the rear of their forces around the Bab al-Mandab Strait leading into the Red Sea by taking control of the heights, which would allow them to open new fronts, according to the sources. That would help protect exposed positions the Houthis captured during their advance around Dhubab on the Red Sea and on Perim Island in the strait. The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen’s capital since 2014, seized the country’s Red Sea coast this month in a lightning advance that routed forces of an internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and based in the south. Saudi plea The New York Times reported that President Trump has changed his strategy on Yemen several times, torn betw­een Saudi pressure to strike the Iran-backed Houthis and the risk of opening another front in the Middle East war. It said Saudi Crown Prince Moham­med bin Salman called Trump on Sun­day “to implore him, again, to step in to help blunt the rapidly advancing group”. Trump had told his advisers the day before that he opposed strikes but chan­ged his mind after the call and “told the Pentagon to prepare for air strikes agai­nst the Houthis”, the newspaper repor­t­ed, citing anonymous administration officials. However, he appeared to have reve­rsed his decision again by midday Sunday, it said. Trump’s decision to pull back from striking the Houthis came as “commanders had approved target lists, troops were loading bombs onto US warplanes selected for the missions and the wave of attacks was just about to begin”, the Times said, citing two people briefed on the operation. US news platform Axios said Trump had already refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis last week. Fox News reported on Sunday that Trump had said the Houthis have agreed not to hit US targets. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Iran shows willingness to return to negotiating table
items.description: • Naqvi meets Pezeshkian, Momeni to ‘discuss mediation process’ • Iran ‘grateful’ to Pakistan’s political, military leadership for peace efforts • US refuses visas to some members of Iranian president’s delegation • Second Qatari LNG cargo ship ‘cleared by Iranians’ due today ISLAMABAD: Iran on Monday indicated its willingness to return to dialogue with the United States to de-escalate tensions. The flexibility on the issue was indicated by the Iranian side during a meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who is in the Iranian capital in an attempt to revive the stalled diplomatic process between Washington and Tehran. “Yes, there was progress during the meeting,” a source told Dawn . Mr Naqvi, who arrived in Tehran on Monday, was received by his Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni. “We had discussions on the mediation process,” Mr Naqvi said while talking to media in the presence of his Iranian counterpart. During the meeting, Mr Momeni said Iran was thankful to Pakistan’s political and military leadership for its efforts for regional peace and stability. “We are grateful to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir for their efforts for regional peace,” the Iranian minister was quoted as saying in a statement issued here by the interior ministry. The visit comes at a time when diplomatic activity has intensified to prevent another round of escalation between Iran and US, with both Qatar and Pakistan maintaining contacts with the two sides. Qatar has in recent we­­eks emerged as a key channel between Wa­­sh­ing­ton and Tehran. Its foreign ministry said on Monday that its mediation team had been exchanging ideas with both sides for nearly two weeks in an effort to bridge differences and find a suitable moment to resume negotiations. Iran relays conditions for talks Iran has conveyed through Qatar a set of conditions for reopening talks, including an end to fighting on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian assets and an end to the US naval blockade. Iranian officials said seven conditions were conveyed, although all of them were not publicly disclosed. The latest diplomatic activity follows the collapse of the 14 point Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding brokered by Pakistan on June 17. The conflict has since continued with sporadic strikes and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran has maintained control over traffic through the strategic waterway. Pakistan, meanwhile, has remained engaged in efforts to keep the diplomatic channel open. Field Marshal Asim Munir has used his contacts with the US administration while Pakistani officials have made repeated visits to Tehran. The latest visit also carries significance ahead of Mr Pezeshkian’s travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. The Iranian president is expected to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the sidelines of the UNGA in the coming days. The meeting could provide another opportunity for the two leaders to discuss the stalled peace process. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has given mixed signals on the prospects of renewed negotiations, while Ira­nian officials have continued to combine their readiness for diplomacy with warnings of a strong response to any fresh US military action. The possibility of renewed diplomacy is also being backed by developments around the Strait of Hormuz, where Pakistan has quietly secured the passage of another Qatari liquefied natural gas shipment after negotiations with Iran. The shipment crossed the strait over the weekend and is expected to reach Pakistan’s LNG import facility by Tuesday, making it the second Qatari LNG cargo to reach Pakistan this month through an understanding with Iran. No visa from US Separately, the US refu­sed to issue visas to members of President Pezesh­kian’s delegation, including his communications team, for his trip to the UN General Assembly, Iranian state media reported. President Peze­shkian will be the highest-ranking Iranian official to enter the United States since the Middle East war began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, part of the delegation to the UN, left Iran on Sunday evening for a stopover in Qatar. Foreign ministry spok­esman Esmaeil Baqaei accused the Trump administration of “trampling on the right of access to information”, pointing to its recent move to bar three major US media outlets from the White House over objections to their coverage. “When an administration slams its doors shut — even on American journalists it happens to dislike — and bars foreign reporters, including the Iranian president’s media team, whose voices it would rather silence, it is not managing access; it is trying to hide the truth,” Baqaei said on X. Iranian airlines to be ‘shut down’ from tomorrow US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Iranian airlines will have trouble functioning globally in two days under the weight of American sanctions. On Sept 23, “all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world,” Bessent told CNBC in an interview as the war launched by the United States and Israel nears the seven-month mark. “If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he added.Two Iraqi sources told AFP on Monday that Baghdad would suspend flights by Iranian airlines following the US Treasury’s announcement. Georgia also barred Iranian carriers from its land, while Iranian airline Mahan said it suspended service to Turkiye at the re­­quest of the Turkish government. Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: PTI bent upon Islamabad march
items.description: • Party will ‘forcefully exercise’ right to protest, scare tactics won’t break their resolve, says CM Afridi • Gohar claims 1,500 party supporters detained, urges govt to review its approach • TTAP denounces detention of lawmakers from Islamabad and KP, demands their release PESHAWAR / ISLAMABAD: As the state swung into action in a bid to deter the opposition party from undertaking its promised protest march on the federal capital, the PTI on Monday vowed to go ahead with its Sept 27 protest , despite the arrest of a number of lawmakers and supporters from different parts of the country. In a press conference at the Chief Minister House in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said the parliamentary committee decided to “forcefully exercise” its right to peaceful protest on Sept 27. The arrest of Imran Khan’s sisters, firing on cabinet minister Shakeel Khan, and the alleged abduction of Labour Minister Fazal Shakoor Khan were aimed at spoiling the party’s protest, the CM said, adding that such tactics would bolster their movement instead of weakening it. CM Afridi claimed that plainclothes men had “attacked and abducted” Minister Shakoor. He also mentioned the reported attempt to “kidnap” the provincial minister for communications, Shakeel Khan, in Batkhela. According to CM Afridi, the PTI has not organised any major protest in the past two years and tried to resolve its issues through assemblies and courts, but to no avail. The chief minister said court orders regarding Imran Khan’s meetings as well as the Supreme Court order about his treatment at Shifa International Hospital were flouted by the government. The PTI leader said holding a peaceful protest was their right, which was guaranteed by the Constitution, adding that they would announce the details of the protest on Sept 25. Speaking at the presser, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan urged the authorities to change their approach. Barrister Gohar said 1500 workers had been detained. “Five of our MNAs have been arrested, along with an ex-senator. Our MPAs have been arrested; one of them was arrested in Islamabad. Even our ministers are being arrested in our own province,” he alleged during a press conference in Peshawar. He said that though the PTI was in power in KP, someone else was calling the shots. He said PTI was a political force and was not looking for violence and clashes but wanted to resolve its issues politically. He said they have approached the high court 25 times and the apex court 19 times over the past four years, but their pleas were not heard. The PTI leader said they were not going to attack Islamabad and such statements by the cabinet members reflected an undemocratic mindset. He claimed people were not concerned about the PTI march, but what worried them was the way the government was talking about stopping the protest. Mr Gohar said that no substantial talks with the government had taken place so far. “They must step back, and we will do the same. But when one side tries to impose its will, that cannot work,” he asserted. Arrests denounced Meanwhile, the PTI condemned the arrests of its lawmakers from Parliament Lodges and outside the National Assembly in Islamabad, calling for their immediate release. In a statement issued by its Central Media Department, the PTI said reports about the detention of MNAs San­aullah Khan Mastikhel, Dawar Khan Kundi, Ahsan Jamal Khan, Mian Ghaus, and Adil Khan Bazai, as well as Chitral MPA Fatehul Mulk were deeply concerning. The arrest of elected representatives from Parl­iament Lodges and outside the National Assembly clearly refle­cted the government’s indiscriminate use of state power to suppress political dissent. Meanwhile, Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan also expressed serious concern over the prevailing political situation in the country, the arrests of political workers, parliamentarians and ordinary citizens, the closure of major roads with containers, and the arrest of sisters of Imran Khan. They urged the government to reconsider its approach, release all detained political workers and citizens, and remove the containers blocking public roads. Two PTI men sent on physical remand An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) in Islamabad remanded two PTI men in police custody for 10 days in a case registered in connection with the party’s Nov 26 protest. ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain passed the order after police produced them before the court and sought their physical remand for interrogation. The investigating officer requested a 30-day physical remand, arguing that the accused were required to be interrogated in connection with the case registered at the Khanna police station. After hearing the arguments, the court granted 10 days’ physical remand and directed police to produce the accused before the court on completion of the remand period. Separately, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra ordered five PTI workers arrested in connection with a February 15 protest on Constitution Avenue to be sent to the Adiala jail for an identification parade. The case was registered at the Secretariat police station against PTI workers and supporters allegedly involved in the protest staged by party lawmakers and activists. In a related proceeding, Judge Sipra ordered Rana Shahbaz, president of the Islamabad Pushcart Vendors Association, to be sent to jail for an identification parade in the same protest case. Police produced Mr Shahbaz before the court and sought his judicial custody for the identification process. The court granted a 14-day judicial remand and directed authorities to produce him again on Oct 5 after completion of the parade. However, Mr Shahbaz’s relatives told the court that he had no affiliation with the PTI and alleged that he was arrested while raising his voice over issues confronting pushcart vendors. The proceedings relate to a case registered with the Secretariat police concerning the PTI’s February protest in Islamabad. Malik Asad in Islamabad also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, September 22nd, 2026

items.title: Despite military might, Saudi struggles to crush the Houthis
items.description: Saudi Arabia has deep pockets and cutting-edge weapons yet for more than a decade it has been unable to quash Yemen's battle-hardened Houthis. The Iran-backed group has now attacked Riyadh with a missile strike, seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast and is blockading Saudi oil exports, seemingly unimpeded. Experts say Saudi Arabia has struggled to rebuff the group in part due to its reliance on ineffective proxies on the ground, while rugged terrain and Iranian support have favoured the Houthis.

items.title: « Jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les lauréates du concours « HAKILI Mousso »
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a reçu ce lundi en audience, les lauréates du concours de détection de talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso », conduite par la Ministre Conseillère spéciale du Président du Faso, chargée du Développement technologique, la Camarade Dr Floriane OUÉDRAOGO/ZONGO. Ce lundi 21 septembre était « jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les filles lauréates du concours national de détection des talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso » et les meilleurs enseignants dans les disciplines scientifiques. Dans cette “salle de classe” d’une heure, ils ont eu droit à une master class du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, sur l’importance des disciplines scientifiques dans le développement. Outre les félicitations pour leur esprit d’abnégation, de surpassement de soi, le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire a prodigué des conseils aux lauréates. Il s’agit entre autres de l’amour des métiers scientifiques, du travail, de la confiance en soi. « Ne vous fixez-pas de limites. Vous êtes capables de tout faire. (…) Demain, nous attendons de vous des ingénieurs en mécanique, mécatronique, électronique, en physique, en astrologie. Vous devez vous donner des objectifs et les atteindre », a dit le Chef de l’État. HAKILI Mousso, un creuset pour l’éclosion d’une élite féminine Le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, a rappelé que le Concours « HAKILI Mousso » ne s’inscrit pas dans la politique du genre importée par les impérialistes avec le dessein d’opposer les femmes aux hommes. « Nous nous inscrivons dans une politique d’élite. Encourager les femmes vers certains métiers qui nous intéressent », a indiqué le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Au cours de cette audience, le Président du Faso a réitéré son engagement pour le développement du Burkina Faso dont la clé de voûte repose sur la qualité des ressources humaines. La première en chimie à « HAKILI Mousso », Inès Marie Fabiolas NIKIEMA est ressortie bien confiante de l’entretien avec le Chef de l’État. Celle qui rêve de faire carrière dans l’aéronautique pour participer à développer son pays, a pris l’engagement de bien travailler et afin d’être un modèle pour les autres jeunes. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso L’article « Jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les lauréates du concours « HAKILI Mousso » est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Révolution Progressiste et Populaire : Ibrahima Maiga interpelle les “révolutionnaires de la 25e heure”
items.description: Depuis les États-Unis, l’activiste burkinabè Ibrahima Maiga a adressé un message incisif aux “révolutionnaires de la 25e heure”, les invitant à respecter les sacrifices des pionniers et à rester focalisés sur la libération et le développement du pays. Ce lundi 21 septembre 2026, à l’occasion du quatrième anniversaire de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, l’activiste burkinabè Ibrahima Maiga, installé aux États-Unis, a livré un message direct aux “révolutionnaires de la 25e heure”, ceux qui ont rejoint le mouvement une fois qu’il avait déjà pris de l’ampleur. Dans son intervention, Maiga n’a pas caché son agacement face à certains comportements : « À force de les voir parler comme s’ils avaient tout vécu, tout porté et tout sacrifié, il y a des moments où j’ai simplement envie de leur rappeler qui était là quand les choses étaient vraiment difficiles. » Il a rappelé que les véritables pionniers sont ceux qui, dès l’an zéro, ont accepté les risques, les critiques et les incertitudes, sans savoir si leurs efforts seraient un jour reconnus. Pour lui, l’histoire ne se raconte pas seulement avec des mots, mais avec des sacrifices, des actes et de la constance. Tout en appelant à garder son calme face aux provocations, Maiga a insisté sur la nécessité de rester concentré sur l’essentiel : « IB n’a pas le temps de s’arrêter sur chaque polémique. Il est focalisé sur la libération et le développement du pays. » Il a également mis en garde contre certains gestes qui, selon lui, ne sont pas innocents et peuvent nuire à l’image du leader. Son message se veut un rappel : ce combat dépasse les ego et les rivalités personnelles. En conclusion, l’activiste a rendu hommage à ceux qui ont porté le poids du combat dès le début, tout en affirmant que chacun, même arrivé plus tard, peut encore contribuer. Mais il a insisté : personne ne doit effacer la mémoire des sacrifices initiaux. « Rester focus. C’est tout. » a-t-il martelé, invitant les révolutionnaires à poursuivre le chemin avec discipline et constance. L’article Révolution Progressiste et Populaire : Ibrahima Maiga interpelle les “révolutionnaires de la 25e heure” est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Denmark, Greenland, US to sign Arctic security agreement
items.description: Denmark, its autonomous territory of Greenland and the United States will sign an agreement in New York on Tuesday to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic region, the Danish Prime Minister's Office said on Monday. The agreement will be signed by Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and US President Donald Trump, according to the office's statement. The signing ceremony is expected to take place at United Nations headquarters at 10:30 a.m. (1430 GMT), on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, the statement said, but did not disclose the agreement's specific terms. Trump announced on social media on Friday that the three sides had reached a deal, saying it would give the United States "permanent control" over Greenland's security. In response, Frederiksen said on the same day that the agreement recognizes the Kingdom of Denmark's sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination. Under a defense agreement signed by Denmark and the United States in 1951 and amended in 2004, the US military already has broad authorization to maintain personnel and facilities in Greenland, including the Pituffik Space Base.

items.title: Pluies au Burkina Fas: Après les invocations, la miséricorde d’Allah se manifeste
items.description: Alors que les pluies se faisaient rares et que certaines semences commençaient à souffrir, de nombreux musulmans ont répondu à l’appel de la #FAIB qui avait demandé de prier en faveur de la pluie, en invoquant Allah pour le retour de la pluie. Depuis vendredi, des pluies sont à nouveau signalées dans plusieurs localités du Burkina Faso, apportant espoir et soulagement aux agriculteurs. Allah dit dans le Saint Coran : « Et Nous avons fait descendre du ciel une eau bénie, avec laquelle Nous avons fait pousser des jardins et le grain qu’on moissonne. » Sourate Qaf (50:9) Qu’Allah bénisse nos terres, fasse prospérer nos récoltes et accorde une saison agricole abondante à tous les agriculteurs du Burkina Faso. Source: Tiwana24 L’article Pluies au Burkina Fas: Après les invocations, la miséricorde d'Allah se manifeste est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina – Niger : un message de solidarité au peuple nigérien
items.description: Une délégation burkinabè, conduite par le camarade général de division, Célestin Simporé, ministre d’Etat, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, et composée de responsables du Burkina Faso et du Mali, a été reçue à Niamey, le vendredi 18 septembre 2026, par le camarade général d’armée Abdourahamane Tiani, Président de la République du Niger. Mandatée par le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, Président du Faso et Président en exercice de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES), la délégation était porteuse d’un message de soutien et de solidarité des peuples burkinabè et malien au peuple nigérien, à la suite des événements survenus récemment à Niamey. Au cours de cette rencontre, la délégation a présenté ses condoléances aux autorités et au peuple nigérien, à la suite des pertes en vies humaines enregistrées lors de la tentative de déstabilisation rapportée les 28 et 29 août 2026. Au cours de cette rencontre, la délégation a présenté ses condoléances aux autorités et au peuple nigérien. Selon le camarade général de division, Célestin Simporé, cette mission traduit la solidarité entre les trois Etats membres de l’AES ainsi que leur volonté de renforcer leur coopération, leur cohésion et leur unité face aux défis communs. En marge de cette mission, la délégation a également salué de passage, les participants à deux ateliers consacrés à l’approfondissement de l’intégration au sein de l’AES. Le premier portait sur l’élaboration d’une convention relative à la portabilité des prestations sociales des travailleurs au sein de la Confédération. Le second était consacré à l’élaboration d’un guide commun pour l’harmonisation des pratiques en matière d’embauche des travailleurs migrants, ainsi que d’un guide du travailleur migrant dans l’espace AES. A travers cette démarche, le Burkina Faso réaffirme, aux côtés du Mali et du Niger, son engagement en faveur de la consolidation de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel, du renforcement de la solidarité entre les Etats membres et de la poursuite de l’idéal commun porté par l’AES. DCRP/MGDP L’article Burkina – Niger : un message de solidarité au peuple nigérien est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina – Djibasso : Le retour des eaux de la rivière « Houwi » ravive l’espoir des producteurs
items.description: Après plusieurs semaines d’attente, le grondement de la rivière « Houwi » a de nouveau résonné à Ourouko, dans la commune de Djibasso, à la faveur de la forte pluie tombée dans la nuit du samedi 19 septembre 2026, ravivant l’espoir des producteurs pour la campagne agricole. A Ourouko, le « Houwi » n’est pas un simple cours d’eau, c’est une rivière qui descend des falaises avant de poursuivre son cours vers le sud et constitue pour les habitants un indicateur naturel de la pluviométrie. Traditionnellement, les populations apprécient l’importance d’une pluie à travers la puissance de l’écoulement de la rivière et le grondement qu’elle produit. Cette année, son réveil était particulièrement attendu. Depuis le début de la saison des pluies, la rivière était restée silencieuse, alors que les habitants avaient l’habitude de la voir couler au plus tard à la mi-juillet. La pluie enregistrée dans la nuit du 19 septembre 2026, considérée par les habitants comme la plus importante depuis le début de la saison dans la commune, a finalement redonné vie au « Houwi ». Dans les champs, l’espoir renaît également. Le petit mil est en floraison, le sorgho en épiaison tandis que les haricots sont en pleine production. Les cultures semblent ainsi bénéficier de cette nouvelle humidité des sols. Pour les producteurs, l’attention se porte désormais sur les dernières semaines de septembre. Ils espèrent encore quelques pluies afin de favoriser la maturation des cultures et de sauver celles semées tardivement, notamment le maïs. Le retour du « Houwi » à Ourouko, est donc accueilli comme un signe d’espoir par les paysans, qui continuent de scruter le ciel pour les dernières pluies de la saison. Agence d’information du Burkina L’article Burkina – Djibasso : Le retour des eaux de la rivière « Houwi » ravive l’espoir des producteurs est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Ouagadougou : Pour une monnaie de 200 FCFA, un client frappe et blesse une restauratrice
items.description: Illustration Reconnu coupable de coups et blessures volontaires sur Dame Sanogo, Zigani a été condamné à 60 mois de prison, dont 24 mois ferme, ainsi qu’à une amende de 500 000 FCFA et au remboursement des frais médicaux de la victime. Le vendredi 11 septembre 2026, la chambre correctionnelle du Tribunal de grande instance de Ouaga I a jugé Zigani, un homme d’une cinquantaine d’années, poursuivi pour coups et blessures volontaires au préjudice de Dame Sanogo, restauratrice. Les faits ont entraîné une incapacité de travail de 45 jours pour la victime. Tout est parti d’une pièce de 200 FCFA jugée trop lisse par Zigani. « C’était dans son restaurant. Après avoir fini de manger, elle m’a remis une pièce lisse de 200 FCFA. Quand je suis parti au travail, je suis revenu chez la dolotière à côté. Je me suis rappelé de ma monnaie et je suis parti la réclamer. Elle m’a jeté l’argent. J’ai protesté et elle m’a jeté de l’eau sale pimentée. Habituellement, on s’amuse ensemble. Il y a eu bagarre et il y a eu des blessures. », explique Zigani. Selon la plaignante, « Il est venu réclamer sa monnaie. Je lui ai remise, mais il a refusé. Il a insulté ma mère. Je lui ai dit qu’on n’insulte pas ma mère. Je l’ai insulté aussi. Il a dit qu’il allait me faire quelque chose. Après, je l’ai vu avancer avec une bouteille cassée alors que j’étais dans la cuisine. Après les faits, j’ai perdu connaissance. » Zigani a reconnu les faits à la barre, tout en affirmant regretter son geste : « C’est l’œuvre du diable » , a-t-il déclaré, expliquant avoir consommé une calebasse de dolo avant l’incident. Le ministère public a estimé que l’infraction était caractérisée et a requis 60 mois de prison, dont 48 mois ferme, assortis d’une amende de 1 million de FCFA. La victime, constituée partie civile, a réclamé 349 114 FCFA pour ses frais médicaux. Dans son délibéré rendu le 18 septembre 2026, le tribunal a condamné Zigani à 60 mois de prison, dont 24 mois ferme, ainsi qu’à une amende ferme de 500 000 FCFA. Il devra également verser à Dame Sanogo la somme de 349 114 FCFA au titre des réparations civiles. Source : Zoodomail L’article Ouagadougou : Pour une monnaie de 200 FCFA, un client frappe et blesse une restauratrice est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: 3 US media outlets file lawsuit after being barred from White House
items.description: Three US news organizations – CNN, MSNOW and Politico – said on Monday that they are suing US President Donald Trump and several White House officials after being barred from entering the White House. "This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the three news organizations said in a joint statement. "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference," the statement continued. The lawsuit, filed in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, also listed Steven Cheung, assistant to the president for communications, Sean Curran, director of the Secret Service, and Susan Wiles, White House chief of staff, as defendants. The latest lawsuit came after Trump said on social media Friday that CNN, MSNOW and Politico were banned from the White House "effective immediately," citing what he called constant "fake news." On Saturday, reporters from the three media outlets were denied entry to the White House, and their press credentials were confiscated. In a social media post, Trump reacted to the latest lawsuit on Monday. "As expected, Fake News CNN, Politico (Pay back the 8 Million Dollar contribution made by the US Government to keep them afloat!), and MSNOW (formerly known as MSDNC!), have brought suit to gain access to the White House, and your President, ME!" Trump said in a post on his social media platform Truth Social. "Almost without question and, as usual, we'll go for appeal," Trump continued, arguing that "Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown 'sources,' shouldn't be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World." Since the beginning of Trump's second term, his relationship with US news organizations has remained tense, with the president frequently criticizing media outlets over what he calls "fake news" and taking legal action against some of them. In February 2025, reporters from The Associated Press (AP) were barred from access to the White House Oval Office, Mar-a-Lago and Air Force One after the AP declined to adopt the Trump administration's renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America." Trump has also filed lawsuits against media organizations including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and CBS, accusing them of defamation or misleading reporting.

items.title: Burkina Faso : La liberté provisoire encore refusée à l’ex ministre de l’éducation Lionel Bilgo
items.description: Le Tribunal de grande instance de Bobo-Dioulasso a rejeté la demande de liberté provisoire de l’ancien ministre Lionel Bilgo et du gérant de SITRAF, Vincent de Paul Kaboré. La suite de la procédure est renvoyée au 5 octobre 2026. Le dossier opposant le ministère public à l’ancien ministre Lionel Bilgo et à Vincent de Paul Kaboré, gérant de la société SITRAF, a de nouveau été examiné devant le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso. Au terme des débats consacrés à la demande de liberté provisoire formulée par les deux prévenus, le tribunal a décidé de maintenir les intéressés en détention. L’affaire a été renvoyée au 5 octobre 2026. À la barre, l’ancien ministre Lionel Bilgo a apporté des précisions sur la période durant laquelle lui et son co-prévenu ont été privés de liberté. « Nos conseils parlent du 28 août comme date de notre détention, mais je précise que c’est dix jours avant le 28 que nous avons été retenus au commissariat central », a-t-il déclaré. L’ancien membre du gouvernement a également évoqué la lenteur de la procédure. Il a expliqué que les prévenus espéraient être entendus le 4 septembre, mais qu’ils avaient finalement appris que des enquêtes complémentaires étaient en cours. Lionel Bilgo a par ailleurs insisté sur leur volonté de collaborer avec la justice. « Nous sommes venus de nous-mêmes », a-t-il notamment déclaré, soulignant qu’ils avaient répondu à des convocations et ne cherchaient pas, selon lui, à se soustraire à la justice. Son co-prévenu, Vincent de Paul Kaboré, a également sollicité la liberté provisoire. Le gérant de SITRAF a mis en avant les conséquences de leur détention sur leurs activités professionnelles et leurs familles. « Nous sommes venus de nous-mêmes. Actuellement, nous ne travaillons pas et nous avons beaucoup de charges de famille », a-t-il plaidé, avant de demander au tribunal d’accorder la liberté provisoire. Le ministère public s’est, pour sa part, opposé à la demande de mise en liberté. Pour le parquet, les garanties de représentation présentées par les prévenus ne seraient pas suffisantes. Le représentant du ministère public a notamment évoqué des précédents dans lesquels des personnes poursuivies, après avoir pris l’engagement de se présenter devant la justice, avaient finalement pris la fuite. Le parquet a ainsi défendu le maintien en détention des deux prévenus. Face à cette position, les conseils de Lionel Bilgo et Vincent de Paul Kaboré ont soulevé des interrogations concernant le calendrier de la procédure et la date à laquelle leurs clients pourraient effectivement être jugés. Les débats ont notamment porté sur l'éventualité de nouveaux renvois ou d'une éventuelle transmission du dossier à une autre juridiction, alors que la demande de liberté provisoire était également rejetée. Après ces échanges, le président de l’audience a suspendu les débats pendant une trentaine de minutes. À la reprise, à 10 h 22, le tribunal a rendu sa décision : la demande de liberté provisoire a été rejetée et l’affaire a été renvoyée au 5 octobre 2026. Lionel Bilgo, ancien ministre de l’Éducation nationale et ancien porte-parole du gouvernement, ainsi que Vincent de Paul Kaboré, gérant de SITRAF, ont été placés sous mandat de dépôt le 28 août 2026. Ils sont poursuivis dans une affaire portant sur des soupçons de spéculation foncière et de vente illégale de parcelles nues sur les sites de Léguéma et Lôgofourousso, à Bobo-Dioulasso. Ils étaient initialement poursuivis pour exercice illégal d’activités de promotion foncière et publicité sans autorisation, en lien avec la loi du 20 juin 2023 portant promotion immobilière. Après une première audience tenue le 4 septembre 2026, l’affaire avait été renvoyée au 18 septembre pour permettre la production de pièces complémentaires. Les débats se poursuivent désormais dans le cadre de la procédure devant le pôle économique et financier (ECOFI), avec une prochaine audience fixée au 5 octobre 2026. L’article Burkina Faso : La liberté provisoire encore refusée à l'ex ministre de l'éducation Lionel Bilgo est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

Chinese FM urges China, Germany to boost cooperation, free trade
items.description: Strengthening mutually beneficial cooperation between China and Germany serves the interests of both sides and is the right choice for both, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday. In a phone conversation with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, called on China and Germany to send a positive signal of jointly upholding multilateralism and free trade, boost confidence in the development of China-Germany relations, and play a constructive role in the development of China-EU relations. Noting that China and Germany are major economies in the world and all-round strategic partners, Wang said that in the face of unilateralism and deglobalization, it is necessary for both sides to strengthen strategic communication, enhance mutual trust and deepen practical cooperation. The two sides should cherish the progress achieved so far, push China-Germany cooperation to greater depth and solidity, and continue to produce new results, Wang said. Wang pointed out that the one-China principle is the political foundation of China-Germany relations. He expressed the hope that Germany would cherish and build on the tradition of mutual trust and friendship between China and Germany, adhere to the one-China principle, and take concrete actions to safeguard China-Germany relations as well as peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait, thereby creating the necessary conditions for high-level exchanges between the two sides. Noting that China and the EU are comprehensive strategic partners, Wang said that the two sides should not fight a trade war. China has consistently maintained that China and the EU should work in the same direction and resolve each other's concerns through dialogue and consultation, Wang said. Wang also expressed the hope that Germany would maintain a rational and practical approach, play a positive role within the EU, and help promote the EU to uphold free trade, reject protectionism, and stay on the right course of openness, cooperation, dialogue and consultation. For his part, Wadephul said Germany-China relations have maintained a sound momentum of development in recent years. Germany looks forward to further strengthening high-level exchanges with China, holding a new round of Germany-China intergovernmental consultations, deepening practical cooperation in areas such as trade and the economy, and continuously advancing bilateral relations, said Wadephul. The German side firmly adheres to the one-China policy and the position will not change, said Wadephul. Noting that the current international situation is facing a series of new threats and challenges, Wadephul said that Germany expects China to leverage its influence in international and regional affairs and work with Germany to explore solutions. Germany supports the EU and China in properly addressing their differences through dialogue and is willing to play an active role in this regard, he added. Wang said an important consensus reached by China and Germany today is that China-EU economic and trade issues should be resolved through dialogue and consultation. The two sides also exchanged views on the situation in Iran and the Ukraine crisis. Wang reiterated China's principled position, saying China will only do what is conducive to peace and remains committed to promoting talks for peace. China stands ready to continue strengthening communication and coordination with the EU and make joint efforts toward this end.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Décès du Professeur Michel Akotionga, pionnier de la gynécologie-obstétrique et défenseur des droits des femmes
items.description: La Société des gynécologues et obstétriciens du Burkina (SOGOB) a annoncé ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 le décès du Professeur Michel Akotionga, ancien président et membre éminent. Pionnier de la médecine, il a marqué des générations de praticiens et consacré sa vie à la santé et à la dignité des femmes. Le Professeur Michel Akotionga, ancien président de la SOGOB, est décédé ce lundi 21 septembre 2026. Figure majeure de la gynécologie-obstétrique au Burkina Faso, il a consacré son existence à la formation des praticiens et à la défense des droits des femmes. Reconnu pour sa rigueur et sa générosité, le Professeur Akotionga a formé des générations de médecins, laissant une empreinte durable dans la profession. Il s’est particulièrement illustré dans la lutte contre les mutilations génitales féminines, mettant son savoir et sa voix au service de la santé et de la dignité des femmes. Ce combat restera un repère pour la communauté médicale et pour le pays. Dans son communiqué, la SOGOB exprime une immense tristesse : « La SOGOB perd un guide, et le Burkina un grand serviteur de la santé des femmes. » Elle présente ses condoléances à la famille, aux proches et à toute la communauté médicale, affirmant que son héritage vivra à travers ceux qu’il a formés. L’article Burkina Faso : Décès du Professeur Michel Akotionga, pionnier de la gynécologie-obstétrique et défenseur des droits des femmes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Grand banditisme et séquestration : la Police Nationale mobilise les citoyens pour capturer le nommé Tighré Jean Pingwendé
items.description: Recherché pour des faits présumés d'enlèvement, de séquestration, d'assassinat, d'association de malfaiteurs et de grand banditisme à Bobo-Dioulasso, Tighré Jean Pingwendé est activement traqué par la Police Nationale. Aperçu dernièrement à Ouagadougou, cet homme évoluant dans le domaine des forages fait l'objet d'un appel urgent à la collaboration citoyenne lancé par les forces de sécurité. La Police Nationale a diffusé un avis de recherche ciblant le nommé Tighré Jean Pingwendé, un individu évoluant dans le domaine des forages. Les forces de l'ordre le recherchent activement pour des faits présumés d'une haute gravité : enlèvement, séquestration, assassinat, association de malfaiteurs et actes de grand banditisme. L'ensemble de ces infractions aurait été commis dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso. L'enquête s'oriente désormais vers la capitale. Selon les dernières informations transmises par les services de sécurité, le suspect aurait été repéré à Ouagadougou. Face à la gravité des faits reprochés, la Police Nationale mise sur le concours de la population pour appuyer l'action des forces de l'ordre. Les autorités appellent à une franche collaboration citoyenne afin de contribuer efficacement à la lutte contre l'insécurité. Toute personne en possession d'informations permettant de localiser l'individu est priée de contacter immédiatement les services de sécurité compétents ou de composer l'un des numéros d'urgence mis en place : 70.30.60.23, 71.11.31.50, 17, 16, 1010, ou d'alerter le service de sécurité le plus proche. L’article Grand banditisme et séquestration : la Police Nationale mobilise les citoyens pour capturer le nommé Tighré Jean Pingwendé est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .
